name: Doi Maach
subtitle: fish poached in whisked yogurt with cardamom and ginger, tangy and pale gold

ingredients.qty: 2 medium, ground to a smooth paste

prepNotes: Rub the fish with 1 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt and rest 15 minutes.
Take the yogurt out of the fridge an hour ahead and whisk it with a fork until there is not a single lump. Cold, lumpy yogurt splits on contact with heat.
Whisk the kashmiri chilli and remaining turmeric into the yogurt now, not into the hot pan later.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool it slightly, then fry the fish steaks 2-3 minutes a side until just set. Lift out.
steps.tip: This is a light fry, not a hard one. The fish finishes in the yogurt.

steps.text: Pour off all but 3 tbsp of the oil. Add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves and let them swell for 20 seconds.
Add the onion paste and fry 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until it is pale gold and no longer smells sharp.
steps.tip: Onion paste spits and catches. Keep the heat at medium and keep the spoon moving.

steps.text: Add the ginger paste and cook 1 minute more.
Take the pan off the heat entirely and let it cool for a full minute.
steps.tip: Adding yogurt to a screaming hot pan is the single reason this dish fails.

steps.text: Add the spiced yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring continuously, until it is all in and smooth.
Return to the lowest heat and cook 5-6 minutes, stirring in one direction, until the gravy thickens and gloss appears on the surface.
steps.tip: Never let it boil. If it looks like it is about to break, lift the pan off the heat and keep stirring.

steps.text: Add 150ml water, the sugar, salt and slit chillies and bring to the barest simmer.
Slide the fish back in, spoon the gravy over, and cook 5 minutes covered.
Finish with the ghee off the heat and rest 10 minutes before serving with rice.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat over very low heat, stirring. A yogurt gravy will split if it is rushed or microwaved.
